decision: POODO is the extensible core; Foundation Math is the first sibling domain extension and outbound capability.

first_slice.publication_scope: Project repository access is managed separately from runtime authority.

core_owns: attempt identity and authoritative append-only ledger

extension_contract.guard: Hooks return data; no mutable core, grant or ledger reference. Core cannot widen a domain acceptance policy.
extension_contract.versioning: Unknown major version rejects. Conformance/migration fixtures required for core/extension changes.

ports.LedgerPort: optional storage seam; bounded in-memory v0.1
ports.EndoforgePort: Future generative UI/disposable software produce, qualify, preview, revise, activate, dispose lifecycle governed by POODO; lower execution backends remain separate. Foundations power generated artifacts; host-owned UI state and exact source/action/revision bindings retained. Not implemented by this first slice.

endoforge_boundary: POODO governs goals, authority, budgets, evidence and acceptance; Endoforge proposes/generates task-specific tools and UI, builds/runs/evaluates/disposes or retains under explicit policy; Foundations supply domain requirements and verifiers. Intended architecture is distinct from currently verified precursor capability.
runtime: Concrete Math adapter may use replaceable process/execution backend; no process or runtime imports in core.
minimal_acceptance: fake unrelated domain exercises inherited lifecycle without Math imports
false identity is completed negative observation not proof
proof_complete instructions do not promote evidence
foundations_role: Domain capability packs power Endoforge-generated UI and disposable software with domain knowledge, exact primitives, constraints and checks; they remain reusable through ports outside Endoforge as well.
illustrative_flow: POODO chooses domain capability contracts and authorized plan
Endoforge synthesizes task UI/software using Foundation capabilities
POODO accepts, rejects, disposes or explicitly retains within policy
flow_constraint: Illustrative composable flow, not a rigid linear stack or transfer of acceptance authority to generated code.
scope_limit: This contract specifies a bounded local prototype, not full autonomous reasoning, current MCP interoperability, formal theorem proving, or hostile-code isolation.
